newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-RUSSIA TO FACE REST OF THE WORLD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RUSSIA TO FACE REST OF THE WORLD.

text.p: Russia will play a Rest of the World team on August 18 to mark the centenary of Russian soccer.
Russian Football Union director general Vladimir Rodionov said the game was agreed with FIFA two months ago but arrangements were only being finalised now.
Barcelona's former coach Bobby Robson has agreed to manage the Rest of the World side. He has sent invitations to 25 players but it was not clear who had accepted.

Those invited included German libero Lothar Matthaeus (Bayern Munich), Mexican defender Claudio Suarez (Guadalajara), France's Franck LeBoeuf (Chelsea) and Jean-Pierre Papin (Bordeaux), Argentina's Gabriel Batistuta (Fiorentina), Italians Gianfranco Zola (Chelsea) and Roberto Baggio (AC Milan) and England's Ian Wright (Arsenal).

"The match is to be played in Luzhniki (Olympic) Stadium which the mayor of Moscow Yuri Luzhkov promised us would be ready. But just in case we are keeping in reserve the 30,000-seater Lokomotiv stadium," Rodionov said.
The giant Luzhniki stadium -- used in the 1980 Olympic Games -- has been equipped with a new retractable roof and will be capable of seating 86,000. Work is nearing completion.
